when: Anytime; review themed pages before interviews

sittings.bodyEn: A large language model predicts the next token after a tokenizer maps text into a vocabulary. The base model holds parameters in layers of self-attention, multi-head attention, and a feed-forward network, with residual connections and layer norm. Embedding vectors sit in a context window; positional encoding or RoPE and a causal mask keep order and stop looking ahead. At decode time, temperature and sampling shape logits, while a KV cache speeds inference. Watch for hallucination, multimodal inputs, MoE routing, and empty claims about emergent ability.

terms.hook: If they say this, they mean the core LLM object most posts name.
If they say this, they mean the pretrained starting point.
If they say this, they mean the unit the model predicts.
If they say this, they mean how much text fits at once.

sittings.bodyEn: Pretraining builds the base model, then supervised fine-tuning teaches instructions. Preference stages use RLHF with a reward model, or DPO on chosen versus rejected pairs. Training minimizes a loss such as cross-entropy, reports perplexity, and updates weights with gradient descent under a learning rate. Watch overfitting, underfitting, catastrophic forgetting, and scaling laws as data and compute grow. Practical knobs include full fine-tuning versus PEFT, LoRA or QLoRA, quantization, data mix, and careful labelling.

terms.hook: If they say this, they mean building the base model from scratch.
If they say this, they mean SFT on instructions after pretraining.
If they say this, they mean the scorer inside RLHF.
If they say this, ask whether they mean full, LoRA, or QLoRA.

sittings.bodyEn: On the product side you write a prompt or system prompt, add few-shot examples, and may ask for chain-of-thought before structured output. Function calling lets the model request tools, and agents use workflows, orchestration, and memory. RAG retrieves from a knowledge base after chunking into a vector database, often with recall, reranking, and hybrid retrieval. Ops language covers AIGC, text-to-image, image-to-video, digital humans, and content or product operations. Close the loop with a PRD, user persona, competitor analysis, schedule, and retrospective.

terms.hook: If they say this, they mean a tool-using loop, not a chatbot slogan.
If they say this, they mean retrieve then generate over a knowledge base.
If they say this, they mean the instructions you give the model.
If they say this, they mean the documents RAG searches.

sittings.bodyEn: On BOSS you apply as a job seeker, sometimes with a referral code. Paths split into daily or summer internship versus full-time campus hiring for fresh graduates or the class of 2027. Screens include a written or machine test before first, second, manager, and HR interviews. Offers arrive as an offer letter or letter of intent, with headcount, base city, daily pay or fifteen salaries, and later conversion to full-time. Foreign students also track the internship endorsement on the residence permit.

terms.hook: If they say this, they mean full-time new-grad hiring—not daily internship.
If they say this, they mean year-round internship seats.
If they say this, the visa clock often starts here.
If they say this, they mean the permit note that makes internships legal.

sittings.bodyEn: Inference means running a trained model; in Chinese the same word can also mean reasoning, so watch context. Deployment puts the model on company servers, and teams watch time to first token, throughput, concurrency, GPU memory, and compute. Cost talk includes open-weight versus closed models and pay-per-use billing. Low-level infra uses operators on chips such as Ascend, plus serving ideas like continuous batching. Say what you have run—MCP and A2A included—not what you have never compiled.

terms.hook: If they say this, check context—running a model or “reasoning”.
If they say this, they mean how fast the first token arrives.
If they say this, they mean VRAM budget during train or serve.
If they say this on infra posts, they mean low-level chip compute.

sittings.bodyEn: Product teams live in a funnel from impressions to buy, and quote click-through rate, completion, engagement, conversion, retention, DAU, and MAU. Commerce adds average order value, GMV, acquisition cost, ROI, creators, livestream selling, and going global. Release safety uses A/B tests and gradual rollout. Model teams speak evaluation, eval sets, regression tests, and recall when retrieval quality matters. Bring one metric you personally moved whenever you claim ops impact.

terms.hook: If they say this, they mean clicks over impressions.
If they say this, they mean the share that completed the goal.
If they say this, they mean a scored test set for the model.
If they say this, they mean shipping to a small slice first.

sittings.bodyEn: Prompt injection hides instructions inside text the system reads, and jailbreak tries to talk the model past its rules. Defenses include guardrails on what an agent may see and do, plus human review before anything goes out. Hallucination is fluent falsehood, so treat it as a product risk. Evaluation, regression tests, and narrow tool permissions limit blast radius when injection wins. Never claim a prompt alone makes a system safe—design so a successful attack cannot move money, spam users, or leak private data.

terms.hook: If they say this, they mean hidden instructions in untrusted text.
If they say this, they mean talking the model past its rules.
If they say this, they mean hard limits on what the agent may do.
If they say this, they mean fluent falsehood treated as fact.

sittings.bodyEn: Interview flow words include textbook questions, live coding, project deep dives, and reverse questions at the end. Workplace talk shows up in HR and PM chats: lever, empower, closed loop, align, granularity, playbook, accumulate, land, connect teams, fallback, chain, mental model, pain point, bottleneck, reuse, iterate, and sync. You do not need to sound fake—just understand them when others speak. Pair each buzzword with one concrete action from your project. If a word is empty, ask for the metric or the next step instead of nodding.

terms.hook: If they say this, they mean standard interview Q&A drills.
If they say this, they mean write code by hand in the interview.
If they say this, they will open the repo and ask why-chains.
If they say this, they mean the questions you ask at the end.
